newsitem.title: USA: Danka buys Kodak office copier business.
newsitem.headline: Danka buys Kodak office copier business.

text.p: Danka Business Systems Plc will acquire the sales, marketing and equipment service operations of Eastman Kodak Co.'s office copier business for $684 million in cash, the companies said Monday.

The companies will also form a strategic alliance whereby Kodak will supply high volume copiers and printers to Danka, making the British-based company the principal distributor of Kodak-branded office copiers and printers.

Kodak will retain manufacturing and research and development functions supporting its office imaging business. Kodak will also retain its key colour electrophotography technology for use in its other imaging businesses.

News of the deal boosted Danka's American Depositary Receipts, which jumped $4.75, or nearly 16 percent, to $34.625 on Nasdaq. Kodak fell 37.5 cents to $71.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
The deal will make Danka a one-stop shop for office copiers and printers worldwide, while expanding the market for Rochester, N.Y.-based Kodak's products.

"This strategic alliance will allow Danka to offer customers a unique combination of unparalleled service and support with global coverage, as well as a wide choice in equipment -- from small copiers to high- volume duplicators, fax machines and state-of-the art digital copiers/printers," said Dan Doyle, chief executive officer of Danka.
"This alliance promises to increase access to the market for Kodak-branded office imaging products," said Kodak's assistant chief operating officer, Carl Kohrt.

"In addition, Danka's acquisition of our sales, marketing, and facilities management operations will place our sales and service people in a growing organisation that is devoted exclusively to providing solutions for the office."
Danka is already one of the largest and fastest growing independent suppliers of automated office equipment and related service and supplies in North America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

The deal should bring Danka's yearly sales to about $3.5 billion and double its recurring revenues from copier service, supplies and rentals to over $2 billion. The company, whose U.S. operations are based in St. Petersburg, Fla., will have 22,000 employees in more than 700 offices in 35 countries.
Under the agreement, Danka will also assume certain assets and operating liabilities of Kodak's Office Imaging as well as its customer-service and distribution organisation.
Kodak will retain $123 million in receivables stemming from long-term copier leases in Britain and Canada.

Danka said it would take a one-time restructuring charge of $25 million to $35 million in its third quarter to integrate the Kodak acquisition, but the purchase should enhance earnings in the first 12 months of operations.

Danka said the unaudited book value of the net assets to be acquired was about $800 million as of Dec. 31, 1995. The assets had net earnings of $20 million on revenues of $1.8 billion in the year ending Dec. 31, 1995.
Danka said it would fund the deal with bank debt under a six-year, $1.2 billion fully underwritten commitment.
Around 10,400 Kodak employees will be offered employment by Danka, of which some 6,000 are located in the United States.
The parties plan to close the deal by the end of 1996, subject to approval by Danka shareholders and regulators.
